\( \text{Worked Solution}\)

\( \text{In order to carry out trig substitution integrals, let's take a look at the information in the table below.} \)

\( \text{If you see }\)

\( \text{Use the following substitution}\)

\(\text{Where}\)

\(\text{So that,}\)

\(\sqrt{a^2-x^2}\)

\(x=a\sin(\theta)\)

\(dx=a\cos(\theta)d\theta\)

\(\sqrt{a^2-x^2} = a\cos(\theta)\)

\(\sqrt{a^2+x^2}\)

\(x=a\tan(\theta)\)

\(dx=a\sec^{2}(\theta)d\theta\)

\(\sqrt{a^2+x^2} = a\sec(\theta)\)

\(\sqrt{x^2-a^2}\)

\(x=a\sec(\theta)\)

\(dx=a\sec(\theta)\tan(\theta)d\theta\)

\(\sqrt{x^2-a^2} = a\tan(\theta)\)

Looking at the numerator of the integrand  \(\displaystyle {@num_func@}\),  it seems we'll need the following trig substitution.

\(\displaystyle x= {@let_x@} \implies d(x)={@diff_letx@}d(\theta)\)

Now let us substitute for \(x\) in the numerator as shown. 

\(\displaystyle {@num_func@}= \sqrt{{@var_num1^2@}({@let_x@})^{2}+{@var_num2^2@}} = {@subst_trig@}\)

Recall that \(\displaystyle \tan^{2}(\theta)+1= sec^{2}(\theta)\), therefore

\( \displaystyle \sqrt{@subst_trig2@}= \sqrt{{@var_num2^2@}(sec^{2}(\theta)) } ={@soln_trig_subst_sec@}= {@soln_trig_subst_sec1*soln_trig_subst_sec2a@} \)

Now going back to the question and substituting everything, we'll have,

\( \begin{align} \displaystyle\int{@question_func@} d(x) &= \displaystyle\int \frac{@num_new_trig_func@}{@denom_new_trig_func@}\cdot{@diff_letx@}d(\theta) \\ &=\displaystyle\int {@new_trig_func@} \cdot {@diff_letx@} d(\theta) \\ &=\displaystyle\int {@new_trig_func*diff_letx@} d(\theta) \end{align} \)

Recall that \(\displaystyle \sec (\theta)= \frac{1}{\cos(\theta)}\) and \(\displaystyle \tan(\theta)= \frac{\sin(\theta)}{\cos (\theta)} \).

We need to substitute for \(\sec (\theta)\) and \(\tan(\theta)\), then simplify the integral as shown below;

\( \begin{align} \displaystyle \int {@new_trig_func*diff_letx@} d(\theta) &= \displaystyle \int {@subst_trig2_expr@}d(\theta) \end{align} \)

We can solve the above integral as follows.

We let \(\displaystyle u={@let_u@} \implies du={@diff_let_u@}d(\theta)\) and substitute it

\( \begin{align} \displaystyle \int {@subst_trig2_expr@}d(\theta) &=\displaystyle \int {@eqn_interms_u@}du \\ &= {@int(eqn_interms_u,u)+c@} \end{align} \)

Replacing back \(u\) with {@let_u@} in the above integral, you'll get,

\( \begin{align} \displaystyle {@int(eqn_interms_u,u)+c@} &={@eqn_interms_trig@}\\ \end{align} \)

Since \(\displaystyle x= {@let_x@} \implies {@tan_trig@}\) and \( \displaystyle {@tan_trig^2@} \)

Recall, \( \begin{align} \displaystyle \tan^{2}(\theta) &=\frac{\sin^{2} (\theta)}{\cos^{2} (\theta)} \\ &= \frac{\sin^{2} (\theta)}{1-\sin^{2} (\theta)} \\ {@rhs_tan_trig@} &= \frac{\sin^{2} (\theta)}{1-\sin^{2} (\theta)} \\ \end{align} \)

\( \displaystyle {@expression@} \)

\( \displaystyle {@sin_theta_solve_expression@} \)

\(\displaystyle \sin (\theta)={@sin_theta_solve_expression_2@}\)

The final step will be to substitute \( \displaystyle{@sin_theta_solve_expression_2@} \) with \(\displaystyle \sin(\theta)\) in \( \displaystyle {@eqn_interms_trig@} \) to get the final answer.

\( \displaystyle {@eqn_interms_trig@}={@tta@}={@ta@} \)

Therefore,

\(\displaystyle \int{@question_func@}d(x)={@ta@}\)
